conviction_note: Nothing found that the market cannot already see. The negative engagement data (Apptopia cancellations +16.6% y/y, downloads -20%, Sensor Tower muted, Nielsen share falling, Sarandos's 'not growing as fast as I want') is all in the Reuters, BMO and Wells Fargo previews. Against it: a post-quarter-end company statement (Oct 14) that the full-year forecast is on track, and a consensus that has come down to the company's own guide. The findings net to -0.5. p_up is 48 rather than 50 because this name has fallen on 6 of its last 7 prints and the Q4 guide carries a new restructuring line. The 25-delta skew of -7.5 says upside is being paid for, and the evidence does not overrule it, so the lean stays slight. abs_move 9.5 is the 9.3 event-implied move rounded up, because the hunters' sizes have run small.
bar: Q3 2026 company guide: revenue $12.86B (+11.7% y/y, ~11% FX-neutral), operating income $4.27B / 33.2% margin, net income $3.45B, diluted EPS $0.82 (Q2 2026 shareholder letter, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001065280/000106528026000211/ex991_q226.htm, 2026-07-16). Consensus is effectively the guide: LSEG revenue $12.87B, EPS $0.82 (via CNBC/Reuters, https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/20/netflix-nflx-earnings-q3-2026.html), and Hudson Labs revenue $12,879M, EPS $0.82 (https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/netflix-q3-2026-earnings-preview-nflx-revenue-guidance, 2026-10-05). FY2026 guide: revenue $51.0-51.4B (narrowed in July), operating margin 31.5%, ads about $3B, FCF about $12.5B; consensus FY revenue about $51.2B (Hudson Labs). Implied Q4 revenue is about $13.3-13.7B. One outlier (TickerDaily: $0.8385 / $13.14B) is disregarded because two agreeing sources plus the company guide sit at $12.87B / $0.82. The line the stock trades on is the Q4 guide, the FY reaffirmation and engagement commentary. No FY2027 guide is expected until January.
positioning_check: Short interest is 82.2M shares as of the 2026-09-30 settlement, 2.1 days to cover (Nasdaq data cited by TheStreet Pro, https://pro.thestreet.com/portfolio/big-netflix-cut-reaffirms-our-growing-concerns, 2026-10-14). That is about 2% of float, down from about 104M at the June 30 peak (FINRA via https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/nflx/short-interest/). It is not a crowded short, so there is no squeeze mechanism. Baseline: 25-delta skew -7.51 vol points (calls richer than puts, 'upside paid'), put/call OI 0.63, ATM IV 114%, event-implied move 9.3%. Spot 69.27 is -44.2% from the 52-week high and +3.3% from the 52-week low, with run-up -4.0% over 20 days and -1.7% over 5 days. The stock has fallen on 6 of the last 7 prints (median |move| 7.26%), and the stock fell five straight weeks into early October. Sell-side: Moderate Buy (18 Buy / 5 Hold / 2 Sell, average PT $87.91 per TipRanks). Pre-print target cuts from Seaport ($102 to $90), BMO ($135 to $125) and Wedbush ($105 to $90); Wells Fargo Underweight, PT $57. Stocktwits retail sentiment was bullish on Oct 1. Read: expectations are washed out but options already pay for a relief move.

findings.finding: Third-party app data shows Q3 US engagement weakening. Apptopia: US Netflix cancellations +16.6% y/y in Q3, about twice the pace of the prior three quarters, with churn moving from about 8% into double digits in Jul-Sep. US/Canada app downloads fell about 20%. BMO says Sensor Tower data points to muted Q3 engagement growth. Jefferies estimates hours per member at 49/month in H1 2026, against 66 in H1 2023. Nielsen's Gauge had Netflix at 7.9% of US TV in June (from 8.3%) and 7.8% in July, against YouTube at 14.2%. Netflix no longer reports subscribers, and Q3 revenue was largely set by the March price increase, so this lands mostly on Q4 guide and engagement commentary rather than on the Q3 revenue line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Engagement and growth worries accompanied the last several prints: Q2 2026 -7.26% (revenue 0.1% below consensus, guide below Street, fewer engagement updates), Q1 2026 -9.72%, Q3 2025 -10.07%. The stock has fallen on 6 of 7 prints since Jan 2025.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced. Reuters carried the Apptopia figures on Oct 19, and BMO and TheStreet Pro carried them on Oct 14-20. The stock is 44% off its high and fell five straight weeks. What remains unpriced is whether management confirms the weakness in the letter or the Q4 guide. If the market had fully priced a guide cut, the skew would be put-bid, not call-bid (-7.5).
findings.independence: Several independent series point the same way: Sensor Tower via BMO (https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/bmo-cuts-netflix-stock-price-target-on-engagement-concerns-93CH-4959644, 2026-10-20), Apptopia via TheStreet Pro (https://pro.thestreet.com/portfolio/big-netflix-cut-reaffirms-our-growing-concerns, 2026-10-14), and Nielsen Gauge (https://www.whats-on-netflix.com/news/netflixs-week-of-disruption-bela-bajaria-out-peter-rice-in-as-1000-jobs-are-cut/). Counterweight: BMO's own consumer survey shows strong positioning, and the company says the FY forecast is on track (separate finding). All are proxies, not company numbers.

findings.finding: On Oct 14, two weeks after Q3 closed, Netflix said with its layoff announcement that it remains on track to hit its full-year forecast ($51.0-51.4B revenue, 31.5% operating margin). The co-CEO memo called the business 'strong'. Q3 books were essentially known by then, so a large Q3 revenue miss or an FY cut is unlikely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 Netflix held its FY margin, narrowed its FY revenue range around the midpoint, and the stock still fell 7.26% (on a 0.1% revenue miss and a Q3 guide below Street). Reaffirmations alone have not been rewarded on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: it was public on Oct 14. But the stock kept trading near its 52-week low ($69-72) after it, and the previews (Wells Fargo, BMO, Reuters) frame the print around engagement risk rather than the reaffirmation. If it were fully priced, the implied move would have compressed below the 7.3% median history, yet it is 9.3%.
findings.independence: Wire reports of the same memo (AP via https://abc30.com/story/netflix-is-laying-off-6-workforce-1000-employees-biggest-round-job-cuts-streaming-giant-years/19938143/, 2026-10-14) give 'business was strong' but not the forecast line, so only one outlet carries the 'on track' wording. Sarandos also said on Sep 30 that revenue grew double digits in every region, but that refers to the latest reported period (https://theprint.in/entertainment/netflix-not-growing-as-fast-as-i-want-says-co-ceo-sarandos/3058732/).

findings.finding: The Oct 14 layoff of about 1,000 employees (about 6% of about 16,000) is the largest in company history. It likely produces a severance or restructuring charge in Q4. Because Netflix guides GAAP operating margin, the Q4 margin guide may carry it and print below a Street model that does not, while 2027 opex falls.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior Netflix restructuring charge in the baseline window. The 2022 cuts of about 450 people were immaterial to guidance.
findings.why_not_priced: No outlet quantified a charge, and the previews quote consensus EPS unchanged at the guided $0.82, so no model visibly carries a Q4 charge. If priced, Q4 EPS estimates would have been cut since Oct 14. Inference only; the size of the charge is unknown.
findings.independence: The headcount figure comes from the same event as https://www.whats-on-netflix.com/news/netflixs-week-of-disruption-bela-bajaria-out-peter-rice-in-as-1000-jobs-are-cut/. That source says no restructuring charge is mentioned. Nothing independently sizes a charge.

findings.finding: Content leadership turnover the week before the print. CCO Bela Bajaria is out, Peter Rice (ex-Disney TV chairman) starts Oct 26, and Puck reports film chief Dan Lin is expected to follow. The call will be the first time management explains the content reset, against a Q3 slate that TheStreet Pro and Reuters-quoted analysts call weak.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None comparable in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it was widely reported Oct 15. What is not priced is the tone of the explanation on the call. A reset framed with a cost plan could be read either way.
findings.independence: Separate reporting: https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/business/netflix-chief-content-office-bela-bajaria-out-peter-rice-in/ and Puck. BMO cites the CCO change as an engagement negative (https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/bmo-cuts-netflix-stock-price-target-on-engagement-concerns-93CH-4959644).

findings.finding: Co-CEO Sarandos said on Sep 30 (the last day of Q3) at Bloomberg Screentime: 'Overall, we're not growing as fast as I want us to'. He added that Netflix is doing things that create headwind to that number. Wells Fargo (Underweight, PT $57) said the remark raises questions about Q3 and 2027. This is management itself flagging slow growth into the Q4 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell to about $67.85 in the five weeks to Oct 1 around these remarks. Growth-deceleration prints (Q2 2026 at 13.4%, the lowest in about three years) drew -7.26%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the stock fell into the remark and is near its low. The residual is whether it foreshadows a Q4 guide toward the low end of the FY range ($51.0B). If priced as a guide cut, consensus FY revenue would sit near $51.0B rather than $51.2B.
findings.independence: https://theprint.in/entertainment/netflix-not-growing-as-fast-as-i-want-says-co-ceo-sarandos/3058732/ (2026-10-01), the same remarks. The Oct 14 'on track' statement cuts against it, so this finding is sized net of that and sits in the opposite direction from finding 2. Engagement weakness is different evidence from the same theme as finding 1, which is why both are small.

findings.finding: Netflix closed its 2026-27 US upfront with ad commitments 'nearly doubled' year over year, which ad president Amy Reinhard called in line with expectations. The company reiterated about $3B of 2026 ad revenue, double 2025. Live-sports inventory, including FIFA Women's World Cup 2027 sponsorships, sold out. This supports Q4 ad revenue and the 2027 growth narrative, which BMO calls the clearest path to US/Canada acceleration.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Ad progress was reiterated in Q1 and Q2 2026 and the stock still fell 9.72% and 7.26%. Ads have not carried a print on their own.
findings.source_date: 2026-08 (MediaPost article 417133; month inferred from article sequence, see bizcommunity copy)
findings.why_not_priced: Public since the upfront close, and 'in line with expectations' by the company's own words, so mostly priced. The residual is any first quantification of ad revenue or 2027 ad commentary on the call.

findings.finding: FX moved between the July guide and now. DXY softened through Jul-Aug (about 100.35 at end-July, 99.55 at end-August), ended Q3 roughly flat versus Jul 1 (+0.2%), then rallied after the Sep 16 Fed hike to 101.61 in early October, its highest since June. Q3 reported revenue gets a slight tailwind from the soft quarter average. The Q4 guide, set at October rates on about 55% non-US revenue, gets a slight headwind that could push FY reported revenue toward the low end.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Netflix has trimmed reported guides for FX before. Not separately identifiable in the baseline reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: Macro-to-company transmission that no preview mentions. Sell-side models update FX inconsistently. The effect is small (well under 1% of revenue), which is why it is filed small.
findings.independence: https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/currency/news/588494 (dollar +1.5% in September, little changed over Q3). This is a proxy; the company has not confirmed any FX effect.

findings.finding: The bar has been reset to the company's own guide. Consensus Q3 revenue of $12.87B and EPS of $0.82 sit at the $12.86B / $0.82 guide, whereas in July Netflix's Q3 guide came in below the Street. Netflix has printed Q2 revenue within about 0.1% of its own guide and operating income slightly ahead, so a Q3 headline in line with or slightly above the bar is the base case, not a stretch.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Netflix's Q2 headline met its own guide and the stock fell 7.26%, because the Street had been above the guide. In Q1 2026 (-9.72%) and Q3 2025 (-10.07%) headline-level outcomes were sold too. The quality of the beat and the guide dominate.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: a bar at the guide is visible to everyone. It matters only in contrast to July's setup, where Street-above-guide produced a headline miss. Because the reaction function has sold in-line prints, it is sized small.
findings.independence: LSEG consensus via https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/20/netflix-nflx-earnings-q3-2026.html agrees. The company guide is in https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001065280/000106528026000211/ex991_q226.htm.

findings.finding: The Q2 2026 letter says Q2 operating income was slightly ahead of forecast because of expense timing. Expenses that slipped out of Q2 land in H2, a small drag on Q3 operating margin against the 33.2% guide, though the guide was set after Q2 closed and likely includes it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin has met or beaten the guide on recent prints and the stock has moved on revenue and guide instead.
findings.why_not_priced: Inside what the company has already guided (the Q3 margin guide was issued with knowledge of the timing), so it is sized toward 0.
findings.independence: This shares the company-guide document with finding 8 but reads a different line (operating expense timing, not the revenue bar). No other source.

outside_window.finding: Peter Rice takes over as Chief Content Officer on 2026-10-26, and any decision on film chief Dan Lin is his. The content strategy reset he brings shows after the exit window.
The Nielsen Gauge for September 2026 (Q3's last month) is published around November, about 6-7 weeks after the month ends, so it lands after the window.

searched_and_found_nothing: Credit-card or panel spending data (Second Measure, Yipit, M Science) for Netflix Q3 2026: nothing public found
Netflix Q3 2026 top-10 or engagement report: the company moved its viewing report to an annual cadence, so there is no H2 report before the print
Nielsen Gauge August/September 2026 Netflix share: not yet published
October 2026 FINRA short-interest settlement: only the Sep 30 figure (82.2M, 2.1 days) found
Warner Bros deal: Netflix walked away in late February 2026 and booked the $2.8B termination fee in Q1, so there is no Q3/Q4 item
8-K or other quiet filing between July 16 and October 20 with new guidance: none found beyond the event-date notice
Analyst upgrades in October: none found; Wedbush, BMO and Seaport cuts only

rejected_candidates.candidate: Sarandos's 'double-digit revenue growth in every region' read as a Q3 data point
rejected_candidates.detail: The article paraphrases it as the latest reported period (Q2), not Q3, so it carries no new Q3 information. It is kept only as context in finding 2's independence field.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Q1 2026 other income of $2.85B and higher Q2 cash taxes from the WBD termination fee
rejected_candidates.detail: Already recognised in Q1/Q2 2026. It has no bearing on the Q3 print or the Q4 guide beyond FCF, which was already restated in July.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Euro-denominated debt remeasurement gain or loss in Q3 other income
rejected_candidates.detail: The dollar was roughly flat from Jun 30 to Sep 30, so the effect is near zero. It rests on the same FX series as finding 7.

rejected_candidates.candidate: March 2026 US price increase (ads $7.99 to $8.99, Standard $17.99 to $19.99) flowing fully into Q3 ARM
rejected_candidates.detail: Already embedded in the company's Q3 guide and consensus. It is the reason finding 1's churn data lands on guidance rather than Q3 revenue, so it is folded into finding 1 and finding 8.

baseline_tension: The engagement evidence is negative and public. The skew (-7.5, calls bid), the low short interest and a washed-out stock near its 52-week low say the market is positioned for relief. The evidence slightly favors the downside but does not justify overruling the skew, so p_up sits only 2 points below 50, and the reaction history (6 of 7 down) is what keeps it below rather than at 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (sign against skew, which is -7.5 with upside paid; short interest checked at about 2% of float and not crowded): shrank the engagement negative from -1.0 to -0.8 and the Sarandos guide negative from -0.5 to -0.4. Neither carries a reason the option market is wrong about this print.

Rule 1 (the reaction function vetoes; this name sold in-line and reaffirmed prints 6 of 7 times): shrank the FY-on-track reaffirmation from +0.8 to +0.6, the bar-at-guide finding from +0.5 to +0.4, and the upfront ad finding from +0.5 to +0.4.
Rule 2 (one-off sized as a fraction of operating profit): restructuring charge from -0.3 to -0.2.
Rule 5 (proxy, filed small with independence saying so): FX and Apptopia/Sensor Tower findings kept small. Nothing dropped.
Rule 6: bar verified to the company guide plus two agreeing estimate sources, so no cap. The Rice start date and the September Gauge moved to outside_window.
p_up, abs_move_pct and expected_move_pct unchanged (48, 9.5, -0.38); the impact_sum is unchanged at -0.5, because the resizes offset.
